source.name: sp_UpsertProducts
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_UpsertProducts
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    BEGIN TRANSACTION;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Update existing products
    -------------------------------------------------
    UPDATE p
    SET
        ProductName = s.ProductName,
        Price = s.Price,
        StockQuantity = s.StockQuantity
    FROM dbo.Products p
    INNER JOIN dbo.ProductImportStaging s
        ON p.SKU = s.SKU;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Insert new products
    -------------------------------------------------
    INSERT INTO dbo.Products
    (
        ProductName,
        SKU,
        Price,
        StockQuantity
    )
    SELECT
        s.ProductName,
        s.SKU,
        s.Price,
        s.StockQuantity
    FROM dbo.ProductImportStaging s
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Products p
        ON p.SKU = s.SKU
    WHERE p.ProductID IS NULL;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Delete removed products
    -------------------------------------------------
    DELETE p
    FROM dbo.Products p
    LEFT JOIN dbo.ProductImportStaging s
        ON p.SKU = s.SKU
    WHERE s.SKU IS NULL;

    COMMIT TRANSACTION;
END;

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_UpsertProducts()
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Update existing products
    -------------------------------------------------
    UPDATE dbo.Products p
    SET
        ProductName = s.ProductName,
        Price = s.Price,
        StockQuantity = s.StockQuantity
    FROM dbo.ProductImportStaging s
    WHERE p.SKU = s.SKU;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Insert new products
    -------------------------------------------------
    INSERT INTO dbo.Products
    (
        ProductName,
        SKU,
        Price,
        StockQuantity
    )
    SELECT
        s.ProductName,
        s.SKU,
        s.Price,
        s.StockQuantity
    FROM dbo.ProductImportStaging s
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Products p
        ON p.SKU = s.SKU
    WHERE p.ProductID IS NULL;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Delete removed products
    -------------------------------------------------
    DELETE FROM dbo.Products p
    USING dbo.ProductImportStaging s
    WHERE p.SKU = s.SKU
        AND s.SKU IS NULL;

    -- Note: The above DELETE logic appears incorrect in the original.
    -- It will never match rows because s.SKU IS NULL in the WHERE clause
    -- but requires a match in USING. The likely intent is:
    -- DELETE FROM dbo.Products p
    -- WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    --     SELECT 1 FROM dbo.ProductImportStaging s WHERE s.SKU = p.SKU
    -- );

END;
$$;
assumptions: Schema 'dbo' exists in PostgreSQL database or will be created
Tables 'dbo.Products' and 'dbo.ProductImportStaging' exist with compatible column types
ProductID is the primary key or unique identifier in Products table
SKU is the business key used for matching between tables
No explicit transaction control needed as PostgreSQL procedures run in transaction context by default
SET NOCOUNT ON has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL and is omitted (PostgreSQL doesn't return row counts by default in procedures)

reviewFlags.reason: The DELETE logic appears to have a logical error in both the original SQL Server code and the conversion. The condition 'WHERE p.SKU = s.SKU AND s.SKU IS NULL' will never match any rows because s.SKU cannot simultaneously equal p.SKU and be NULL. The original SQL Server code has the same issue. The likely intent is to delete products that don't exist in the staging table. Consider using: DELETE FROM dbo.Products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.ProductImportStaging s WHERE s.SKU = p.SKU);

reviewFlags.reason: SQL Server's explicit BEGIN/COMMIT TRANSACTION was removed because PostgreSQL procedures automatically run within a transaction context. If explicit transaction control is needed (e.g., for savepoints or autonomous transactions), this should be reviewed and potentially refactored.
PostgreSQL uses different syntax for UPDATE FROM and DELETE USING compared to SQL Server. Verify that the join conditions are correctly translated and produce the expected results with test data.

compatibilityNotes.description: PostgreSQL procedures (PROCEDURE) automatically run in a transaction context. The explicit BEGIN TRANSACTION/COMMIT TRANSACTION from SQL Server is implicit. If the caller needs to control transactions, they should do so outside the procedure.
PostgreSQL does not have an equivalent to SET NOCOUNT ON. PostgreSQL procedures do not return row counts to the client by default, so this difference should not affect behavior.

PostgreSQL uses UPDATE...FROM and DELETE...USING syntax instead of SQL Server's UPDATE/DELETE with table aliases in the FROM clause. The logic has been converted but should be tested to ensure identical behavior.

The original procedure has no explicit error handling (TRY/CATCH). In PostgreSQL, any unhandled exception will automatically roll back the transaction. If specific error handling is needed, add EXCEPTION blocks.
